points.text: Add $\text{AgNO}_{3}$; $\text{Cl}^{-}$ gives a white ppt and $\text{I}^{-}$ gives a yellow ppt
Add $\text{NH}_{3}(\text{aq})$; ppt dissolves and ppt is insoluble
conductivity decreases during the reaction AND number of $\text{Na}^{+}$ / $\text{I}^{-}$ ions are decreased / used up (from solution)
(Equilibrate) solutions at $40\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ / with a water bath (cannot be after mixing)
mix known volumes and start the clock / timing clearly mentioned / implied
measure conductance / conductivity at regular intervals / every measured time [method A] OR measure the time for conductance to go to zero / a specific value / to be constant [method B]

prepare a curve of conductance vs. time [related to method A] OR prepare a curve of conductance vs. concentration [related to method A] OR repeating the experiment at different concentrations [related to method A and B]
[R-$\text{Cl}$]: rate increases by 5 / 3 when concentration increases by 10 / 6 (5 / 3), so order = 1
[$\text{I}^{-}$]: rate increases by 5 / 3 when concentration increases by 5 / 3, so order = 1
$\text{C-Cl}$ dipole AND $\text{C-Cl}$ curly arrow for either $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ or $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism
intermediate cation OR 5-valent transition state (charge essential)
$\text{I}^{-}$ with lone pair AND other curly arrow

If $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ in 2(d)(i) mixture of / two optical isomers will be formed AND the intermediate can be formed by the $\text{I}^{-}$ approaching from top or bottom plane OR if $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ in 2(d)(i) one optical isomer AND attack always from fixed direction / opposite side
